items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 24:1
items.html: The light of Malchut — which means the screen and the reflected light included in it — when it is refined and rises to the Emanator, passes through all the Sefirot; and as it passes within them it is included from all the records that remained in them from their lights, except for the last phase. Therefore, when it reaches the Emanator, that is, Malchut of the Rosh [head], from which the coupling never ceases, it too is found included in that coupling and receives from there coarseness of from below upward, whereby the records in it are again awakened and thickened in their own coarseness, which is from above downward. And then the screen descends to its place in the Guf [body], to the place of the Chazeh [chest]; and from the Chazeh upward it brings out the ten Sefirot of the Rosh, and from the Chazeh downward it expands again into the ten Sefirot of the Guf, as at first. And this is called the second expansion, or the second Partzuf, since it differs from the first Partzuf: for the matter of the vessels of the first Partzuf is from the whole coarseness of phase four, whereas the matter of all the vessels of this second Partzuf is from the coarseness of phase three. The reason is that the screen that rose to Malchut of the Rosh included nothing of the coarseness of phase four, because she left no record after her departure. (Chapter 3, Inner Light, Item 1)
